newsitem.title: UK: Venezuela harbour master refuses to release tanker.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela harbour master refuses to release tanker.

text.p: A Venezuelan harbour master has refused to release a detained oil tanker, despite its arrest being lifted, until he receives instructions relating to fishermens' pollution claims, the ship's owner's representative in London said Monday.
The spokesman for the Greek owners of the Nissos Amorgos said the local Cabimas court had lifted its civil and criminal arrest orders on the vessel late on Friday.

However, he said the harbour master at Punto Fijo, who has jurisdiction over the 89,427 dwt vessel which has been held since it spilled about 25,000 barrels of oil in the Lake Maracaibo shipping channel at the end of February, has said he will not release the vessel.
The harbour master is waiting for instructions from a Caracas court dealing with damages claims of at least $130 million lodged by fishermens' union Fetrapesca, he said.
Venezuela's attorney general suspended charges relating to the grounding and oil spill on June 19.

A spokesman for Ince and Co, lawyers for the ship's owner, said the Cabimas court had accepted that pollution claims would be covered by two international conventions Venezuela has signed. He added that all Venezuela's courts should comply with the judgement.

Ince and Co have also applied for temporary permission for the ship's master to leave the country on compassionate grounds. He will pledge to return if charges are laid against him, the spokesman said. -Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
